items.title: 68003_Eddie Sauter oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...you've probably heard things that Bob Gretinger did for Kenton's Innovation band...

ctx.x: done by the individual per se, it's always a result of a mixture-a social mix. The talent has to be there but it's a variable way, depending on how the environment is working with you. I think that's true of everybody involved with anybody that has to do with this sort of thing.

I've found it curious in the past year or two as I've been investigating things, say that people like George Handy did thirty years ago, or you've probably heard things that Bob Gretinger did for Kenton's Innovation band, things like "City of Glass", and it's interesting to me that there are people like you and Handy and Gretinger who, in a span of maybe ten years, produced this body of "jazz" or "jazz works", or things that were at least written for a jazz band, that you're really influenced by concert music.
